title: Survey error: sampling, clustering, and nonresponse
dek: The sampling design is part of the likelihood (or of the Horvitz–Thompson weights). Pretending a cluster survey is iid is how SEs shrink and maps lie.
story: A TB prevalence survey is usually stratified, clustered, and weighted. Each person has an inclusion probability π_i. The Horvitz–Thompson total is ∑ y_i / π_i. Software that runs an unweighted iid logit on the same rows estimates a different functional — the superpopulation of listed respondents, not the finite-population mean the protocol wrote.

Clustering (enumeration areas, households) induces positive correlation. Design effect DEFF ≈ 1+(m−1)ρ again. Report SEs that use the clusters as the resampling units (sandwich, bootstrap of PSUs, or a mixed model). n = 50,000 individuals with 400 clusters is not n = 50,000 for a district mean.

Nonresponse is not missing completely at random because households that refuse may differ in disease and in risk. Weights and imputation are models of that missingness. A 70% response rate with silence in the methods is a bias story, not a precision story.
deepTitle: Weights, models, and the two populations
deep: Design-based: inference is over the randomisation of the sample from a finite population. Model-based: a superpopulation model for Y, with the design maybe entering via weights or as part of the likelihood (cluster random effects). You can use both; you cannot ignore both.

Weights in a GLM: weighted IRLS estimates a weighted score. That can target a census mean. It is not the same as a mixed model of clustering. People often need both: weights for unequal π_i, clusters for SEs.

Stratification, if used in selection, should appear in the analysis (strata as fixed effects or as part of the survey design object). Post-stratification after the fact is a calibration model — useful, and another assumption.

Lab surveys of isolates inherit the clinic’s sampling: only diagnosed, only cultured, only sequenced. That is a survey error stack on top of the household survey stack. Transmission-genomics caveats were this problem in a different coat.

example.title: 400 clusters, 50,000 X-rays, iid logit
example.setup: National TB prevalence survey. Analyst fits an unweighted iid logit of X-ray-suggestive TB on age and sex, prints p < 10^{-12} for age.

steps.title: Wrong n
steps.body: SEs use n = 50,000. With ρ even 0.02 and m ≈ 125, DEFF is huge. Age may still matter; the stars are theatre.

steps.title: Wrong mean
steps.body: If urban clusters were oversampled, unweighted age coefficients mix a sampling artefact. Use weights for the finite-population regression functional, or a model that includes the design variables.

steps.title: Minimal adult analysis
steps.body: Survey-weighted estimator + cluster-robust SEs at PSU, or a hierarchical model with PSU random intercepts plus weights as a sensitivity. Print the number of PSUs next to every interval.

example.takeaway: The design is data. Weights change the mean; clusters change the SE; nonresponse changes both.

check.prompt: Analysing a cluster survey as iid Bernoulli rows typically:
choices: Leaves point estimates and SEs untouched
Understates SEs (and may also bias means if inclusion probabilities vary)
Is required by the Horvitz–Thompson theorem
check.answer: Understates SEs (and may also bias means if inclusion probabilities vary)
check.why: Ignored ρ and ignored π_i. HT exists because π_i is not equal.

check.prompt: Two people, π₁=0.5, y₁=1; π₂=0.1, y₂=0. A sketch HT total ∑ y/π equals:
check.why: 1/0.5 + 0/0.1 = 2. The rare-inclusion person would have contributed more had y₂ been 1. Unweighted total of observed y is 1.

check.prompt: On the survey hierarchy, missingness is its own layer. Why not fold it into “persons” silently?
choices: Because nonresponse is a missingness mechanism that can bias means, not only a smaller n
Because refusing people have π_i = 1 always
Because HT sets missing y to 0 without comment
check.answer: Because nonresponse is a missingness mechanism that can bias means, not only a smaller n
check.why: The plate is an error stack. Precision and bias live on different layers.

whyWrong.Because HT sets missing y to 0 without c: That would be a bad estimator, not HT as defined for the sampled units.
